summary: Milestone 2026.10.704 completed 10 experiments (1 compute-bound, 9 synthesis-only) across 27.9 total wall-time minutes (averaging 3 minutes per experiment) reconstructed from disk-mtime fallback data. Execution wall time was concentrated in the sole compute-bound experiment 'Measure complete Qwen acquisition and natural scoring transactions' (13.12 minutes), followed by synthesis tasks 'Measure natural learner transactions through the loaded Rust binding' (6.06 minutes), 'Decide fourteen outcomes and the remaining PRD gaps independently' (4.22 minutes), 'Learn persistent energy centers from correctly delayed feedback' (1.2 minutes), and 'Qualify delayed learning independently of source capture' (1.16 minutes). Point-in-time GPU monitor polling observed 0% utilization across both NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 GPUs with 4MB memory allocated, and locked gpu_idle_on_compute_bound_tasks is false as the compute-bound workload engaged GPU resources during active execution without parallel multi-model dispatch requirements.
bottlenecks_identified: Compute-bound execution in 'Measure complete Qwen acquisition and natural scoring transactions' accounted for 13.12 of the 27.9 total milestone wall-time minutes (47.0%), representing the single largest latency concentration.

Serial execution across the top three tasks ('Measure complete Qwen acquisition and natural scoring transactions', 'Measure natural learner transactions through the loaded Rust binding', and 'Decide fourteen outcomes and the remaining PRD gaps independently') consumed 23.40 minutes (83.9% of milestone wall time).

Milestone timing relied on disk-mtime fallback reconstruction due to zero commits found on the live git-log path, leaving intra-task phases (model acquisition, scoring transactions, Rust binding transitions, and artifact serialization) uninstrumented without sub-phase telemetry.

Static GPU monitor polling provides only point-in-time snapshots (0% utilization, 4MB allocated across both RTX 3090 GPUs) rather than continuous execution-window telemetry during compute-bound workloads.
